question.text: Mr. Karan Mehta is evaluating whether to set up Satpura Market-Neutral Fund (Cat III AIF) as an LLP versus a trust. Which is a GENUINE disadvantage of the LLP form relative to a trust?

answer.text: An LLP cannot register as an AIF under SEBI Regulations
LLP attracts joint and several liability on all partners including investor-partners
LLP details including partner (investor) names are filed with the MCA and fall in the public domain, compromising investor confidentiality
LLP form prohibits the manager from charging any performance fee

explanation.text: The Logic: Under the LLP structure, every investor becomes a partner and their names are recorded in the LLP deed filed with the Ministry of Corporate Affairs. These filings are in the public domain — so investor confidentiality is lost. The trust form keeps this information private. LLP also has higher compliance requirements: every investor entry/exit needs a deed amendment and MCA update. The Trap: Option A is wrong (LLP IS permitted). Option B is wrong: LLP limits partner liability to agreed contribution, no joint-and-several liability (that is a general partnership, not an LLP). Option D is fabricated — nothing prohibits performance fees. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C and XIX-D both test LLP downsides. XIX-A/B distributors must disclose the entity form to prospective investors. Manager's Pro-Tip: High-profile Cat III investors — family offices, large corporates — almost always insist on trust form specifically to keep their names off MCA filings. Flag this in your PPM discussion with anchor LPs.
